core.title: Use the optional feature kind: feedback-loop only for producer->consumer correction loops
core.given: You are authoring or editing a feature that carries (or will carry) an explicit optional `kind:` field, which classifies the feature's system archetype — including edits to the behaviour of an already-marked feature where `kind:` itself stays unchanged.
core.when: You save the feature with an explicit `kind:` present.
core.then: The explicit `kind:` must be `kind: feedback-loop`, and the feature's behaviour must be a producer->consumer correction loop: a producer detects a condition and emits, a consumer receives and reacts, and the detecting predicate then no longer fires.
prefer: Write exactly `kind: feedback-loop` — the only valid explicit value of feature_kind.
Leave `kind:` absent for any feature that is not a correction loop; absence means producer-only and no kind validator activates.

When editing an already-marked feedback-loop feature, re-check that the edited behaviour still closes the loop: the producer detects a condition and emits, the consumer receives and reacts, and the detecting predicate then no longer fires.
avoid: Marking a producer-only feature (no consumer reaction closing the loop) as `kind: feedback-loop`.
Writing any explicit `kind:` value other than `feedback-loop` (including `producer-only`, which is the default when the field is absent rather than a listed valid value).
Skipping the check because you edited behaviour but not the `kind:` line of an already-marked feature.
core.why: Feature kind classifies the system archetype; validators activate only for explicitly-marked kinds, so the optional field lets marked loops be validated while existing (unmarked) features are unaffected.
evidence: Every feature with an explicit `kind:` (after any create or edit) has the value `feedback-loop`, and its behaviour is a correction loop — the producer detects a condition and emits, the consumer receives and reacts, and the detecting predicate then no longer fires (judged for every explicitly marked feature, including incorrectly marked non-loops).
Features without `kind:` are treated as producer-only and are not flagged by kind validators.
verification: The check validates the rule term feature_kind (the feature's system archetype): the only valid explicit value is `feedback-loop`; when the field is absent the feature defaults to producer-only.

The `kind:` field is optional: kind checks activate only for features that explicitly carry it (presence in the resulting feature, regardless of whether the current edit touched the field), so features without an explicit `kind:` must never be flagged and existing unmarked features are unaffected.

Whether an explicitly marked feature's behaviour really closes the correction loop (a producer detects a condition and emits, a consumer receives and reacts, the detecting predicate then no longer fires) is judged only after activation, for every explicitly marked feature — including incorrectly marked non-loops, which are checked and flagged.

values: resulting feature has an explicit `kind:` field present (any value, newly added, changed, or unchanged)

fires: A planner writes a new feature that explicitly includes a `kind:` field (any value).
A planner adds or changes the `kind:` value on an existing feature.
A planner edits the behaviour (detection, emission, consumer reaction, acceptances) of a feature that already carries an explicit `kind:` field, even though `kind:` itself is unchanged.
A feature explicitly marked `kind: feedback-loop` whose behaviour is not actually a correction loop is authored or edited — it must still be checked (and flagged).
doesNotFire: A feature, new or existing, that has no `kind:` field after the edit — it defaults to producer-only, the field is optional, and kind validators do not activate, whether or not its behaviour is a loop.

neutralityNotes: This planner rule governs methodology-level artifacts: the feature specification, its optional `kind:` field, and the term feature_kind (valid value `feedback-loop`, absent-field default `producer-only`) are defined by the ATDD convention itself, not by the Bun stack, so the core transfers them nearly verbatim. The only profile dependency is resolving the neutral artifact kind 'feature' to the stack's concrete planner-artifact kinds (roles.plan_artifact.kinds); no path, suffix, tooling or language appears in any agent-facing item. The core activation facts drop the Bun notes (the core schema has no note field); their substantive scope — presence-based activation including behaviour edits that leave `kind:` unchanged, and loop-ness being judged only after activation — is preserved in given and in the verification array. The single bunOnly remnant is the '(issue #825)' provenance pointer in verifier_detail[1], which carries no obligation. Wording note: the Bun shorthand `receive+react` (prefer[2], evidence[0]) was rendered as `the consumer receives and reacts`, matching the core obligation's own accepted phrasing, so no stack/framework-named token remains in any core field.
